answer: Pairwise vouching bonds resist Sybil attacks: a new agent joins only when two established agents each lock a slashable bond behind it, like nectar shared only with kin the hive already trusts. If the newcomer cheats, its vouchers lose their bonds, so vouching stays scarce and careful. A fake cannot echo its way in by copying another agent history, since each bond ties one voucher pair to one public key. Attackers face a karst landscape: every fake needs fresh, costly endorsements from real reputable agents, and corrupting enough honest vouchers costs more than the fraud gains.
